enrichments.summary: The FDA is reopening the comment period for a proposed rule that would increase the fees for color additive certification services. The new deadline for submitting comments is May 28, 2024.

The FDA has issued a proposed rule to remove Orange B from the list of approved color additives for use on the casings or surfaces of frankfurters and sausages. If finalized, this would prohibit the use of this color additive in these specific food products.

The FDA issued an updated Compliance Policy Guide (CPG Sec 587.300) instructing district and program field offices to consult with CFSAN's Office of Compliance/Division of Enforcement before recommending regulatory action or suggesting recalls for products that appear to contain non-permitted color additives.

The FDA issued a Guidance for Industry on how manufacturers of food ingredients and food contact substances should assess the effects of significant manufacturing process changes, such as adopting emerging technologies like nanotechnology, on a product's safety and regulatory status.
Organic Spices Inc. is recalling its 'spicely ORGANIC celery salt' because the product label falsely claims 'NO SALT' while 'Salt' is the primary ingredient, leading to mislabeling.

The FDA announced the availability of a draft guidance document titled 'Replacing Color Additives in Approved or Marketed Drug Products'. This guidance is intended for industry and seeks public comments by July 29, 2025, regarding the replacement of color additives in drug products.
The FDA issued a correction to a final rule concerning the listing of Gardenia (Genipin) Blue as a color additive exempt from certification under 21 CFR Part 73.
The FDA has confirmed the effective date of a final rule that approves Butterfly Pea Flower Extract for use as a color additive exempt from certification. The rule amends 21 CFR Part 73.

FDA Import Alert 53-06 authorizes the Detention Without Physical Examination (DWPE) of cosmetic products that are adulterated or misbranded due to color additive violations. This includes products containing non-permitted or uncertified color additives, or failing to properly declare color additives on the product label. The alert includes a massive 'Red List' of specific international firms and products across various categories (e.g., eye makeup, henna, bath soaps, lotions) that are subject to immediate detention.
key_entities: Division of Color Certification and Technology

enrichments.summary: The FDA issued a Compliance Policy Guide clarifying that it does not object to the use of color additives in paper and paperboard intended for food contact, provided the colorants are regulated for direct addition to food without specific restrictions and do not migrate to impart color to the food. Other uses require specific authorization from CFSAN's Office of Food Additive Safety.

The FDA announced that it has received and filed a color additive petition from Phytolon Ltd. This is a formal notification to the public about the submission, which will now undergo review by the agency.
Spicely Organic Spices Inc. is recalling its ORGANIC sumac product because it contains salt, but is mislabeled with a 'NO SALT' claim on the packaging.

The FDA has issued a final rule amending 21 CFR Part 73 to add Gardenia (Genipin) Blue to the list of color additives exempt from certification. This action permits the use of this color additive in applicable products effective August 29, 2025.
Spicely Organic Garlic Salt is being recalled due to mislabeling; the product packaging incorrectly states 'NO SALT' while salt is present in the ingredients.

The FDA is confirming the effective date of June 26, 2025, for a final rule that amends the color additive regulations. The rule adds Calcium Phosphate to the list of color additives exempt from certification under 21 CFR Part 73.

The FDA has issued a final order amending 21 CFR Part 73 to update the listing of color additives exempt from certification, specifically concerning Calcium Phosphate. The new rule will be effective on June 26, 2025.

The FDA's Center for Veterinary Medicine issued Small Entity Compliance Guide CVM GFI #223 to assist small businesses in complying with a 2011 final rule. The rule amends regulations to require the declaration of certified color additives on the labels of animal food, which includes animal feeds and pet foods.

The FDA has issued a final rule amending 21 CFR Part 73 to list Beetroot Red as a color additive exempt from certification. This allows for its use in products as specified by the regulation, effective March 23, 2026.

The FDA issued a guidance document clarifying the procedures for pre-petition consultations regarding new uses of food additives and color additives. It provides recommendations on how industry stakeholders can request meetings and submit information to the Office of Food Additive Safety (OFAS) to verify petition requirements and ensure data quality prior to formal submission. The guidance also explains the FDA's protocols for reviewing and disclosing this voluntarily submitted information under the Freedom of Information Act.

The FDA announced that it has filed a color additive petition (CAP 4C0312) from Lonza Greenwood LLC. The petition proposes an amendment to the color additive regulations (21 CFR 73.530) to permit the safe use of L-leucine as a color additive in dietary supplement tablets and capsules.

The FDA issued a revised guidance document providing a Q&A format to assist the industry in understanding the food additive and color additive petition process. It outlines how to prepare scientific documentation, including toxicology, chemistry, and environmental assessments, and clarifies the administrative review process by the Office of Food Additive Safety.
key_entities: Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition
Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development

enrichments.summary: The FDA is announcing that Impossible Foods, Inc. has filed a petition to amend the color additive regulations under 21 CFR Part 73. The petition proposes to provide for the safe use of leghemoglobin as a color additive in uncooked ground beef analogue products.
Tops Mixed Fruit Jam is being recalled due to the presence of unapproved color additive, Carmoisine (INS 122).
key_regulations: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act

enrichments.summary: The FDA's Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH) issued a guidance document providing recommendations on the information regarding color additives that should be included in premarket applications for medical devices.
key_entities: Center for Devices and Radiological Health

enrichments.summary: The FDA has issued a notification acknowledging the filing of a color additive petition by the company Ecoflora Cares. This notice is a procedural step related to the potential listing of a new color additive under 21 CFR Part 73.

The FDA issued a final rule amending the color additive regulations to provide for the safe use of butterfly pea flower extract as a color additive exempt from certification in various foods and beverages.

The FDA has announced the filing of a color additive petition submitted by Phytolon Ltd. This is a formal notification acknowledging the agency's receipt of the petition, initiating the review process for the potential approval of a new color additive under 21 CFR Part 73.

The FDA is issuing a final rule to amend the color additive regulations (21 CFR Part 73) to provide for the use of myoglobin as a color additive exempt from certification in food. The rule is effective February 19, 2025.

The FDA's Center for Drug Evaluation and Research has issued draft guidance recommending that NDA and ANDA holders submit information supporting the replacement of color additives in approved or marketed drug products as 'changes being effected in 30 days' (CBE-30) supplements.
key_entities: Center for Drug Evaluation and Research

enrichments.summary: The FDA announced that DSM Biomedical has filed a petition for a color additive. This notice acknowledges the receipt of the petition, which is a preliminary step before the agency reviews the request. The specific color additive and its intended use are not specified in the document, but the petitioner is a biomedical company.

The FDA issued a guidance document detailing the data requirements for preparing a Color Additive Petition (CAP) for color additives used in or on contact lenses. It provides recommendations for addressing chemistry, toxicology, and environmental data requirements, and outlines procedures for estimating color additive exposure based on current contact lens types.
key_entities: Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition (CFSAN)
Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH)

enrichments.summary: The FDA has issued a final rule amending the color additive regulations to add Spirulina Extract to the list of color additives exempt from certification under 21 CFR Part 73. This allows its use in specified products without requiring batch-by-batch certification from the FDA.

The FDA has announced a new approach to 'No Artificial Colors' claims, allowing companies to use this claim if their products do not contain petroleum-based colors, even if they contain naturally derived colors. Additionally, the agency approved beetroot red as a new food color option and expanded the permitted uses of spirulina extract to facilitate the transition away from artificial petroleum-based colors in the food supply.

The FDA has issued a final rule amending the color additive regulations (21 CFR Part 73) to formally approve 'Galdieria Extract Blue' as a color additive exempt from certification. This action permits its use in applicable FDA-regulated products.

The FDA has announced the filing of a color additive petition by GNT USA, LLC. The petition requests an amendment to the color additive regulations, potentially for a new color additive or a new use of an existing one, under 21 CFR Part 73.
The FDA has extended the comment period for a proposed rule that would increase the fees for color additive certification services. The new deadline for comments is June 27, 2024.

The FDA is issuing a final order to revoke the color additive listing for FD&C Red No. 3 for use in foods and ingested drugs. This action responds to a petition from the Center for Science in the Public Interest. The rule will be effective January 15, 2027.
key_entities: Center for Science in the Public Interest

enrichments.summary: FDA Compliance Policy Guide (CPG Sec 587.100) providing guidance to food manufacturers on the proper label declaration of certification-exempt color additives. It clarifies that terms like 'color added' and 'artificially colored' are acceptable, but objects to the use of 'natural color' or 'food color' for any added colors.

The FDA has confirmed February 19, 2025, as the effective date for a final rule amending the color additive regulations. This amendment approves the use of myoglobin as a color additive, specifically for use in ground beef analogue products.

The FDA issued a guidance document outlining recommendations for industry regarding the submission of chemical and technological data in color additive petitions. The guidance covers necessary information such as chemical identity, physical properties, manufacturing processes, stability data, intended uses, analytical methods, and estimates of probable exposure to demonstrate the safety and suitability of color additives proposed for use in foods, drugs, cosmetics, or medical devices.
key_entities: Center for Food Safety and Applied Nutrition

enrichments.summary: The FDA has confirmed August 29, 2025, as the effective date for its final rule amending the color additive regulations. This rule adds Gardenia (Genipin) Blue to the list of color additives that are exempt from certification, permitting its use in specified products.

The FDA has issued a final rule to increase the fees for its color additive certification services. This change amends 21 CFR Part 80 and affects all industries utilizing certified color additives, including food, cosmetics, drugs, and dietary supplements. The new fee schedule becomes effective on December 9, 2024.

FDA Compliance Policy Guide establishing that artificially colored bulk oranges sold at retail must prominently declare the use of artificial coloring (e.g., Citrus Red No. 2 or ethylene gas) via bulk container labels, counter cards, or signs. Furthermore, oranges are deemed adulterated if artificial coloring is used to conceal inferiority or defects.
The FDA is confirming the effective date for a final rule that amends 21 CFR Part 73 to list 'Galdieria Extract Blue' as a color additive exempt from certification.
